name: Buchaechum (Foundation)
notes: Buchaechum foundation pack (Doc 04 template; foundation-forward). The Korean fan dance — and the catalog's cleanest credit: buchaechum was CREATED IN 1954 BY KIM BAEK-BONG, a named woman choreographer who drew on shamanic ritual aesthetics and court dance to build a new work that became a national icon; her name and her academy's lineage travel with every performance, and this pack says so in curriculum (a living counter-example to 'folk dances have no author'). Design truths: the iconic imagery — flowers, waves, butterflies blooming from massed fans — is ENSEMBLE art, so the group forms are 🤝 and the pack is honest that the full dance lives with teams and teachers (Korean cultural centers and dance academies worldwide); what solo practice honestly owns is real and lovely: the breath-led vertical rhythm (the Korean aesthetic of 'heung' — the lift of joy — described with humility), the curved line, walking in stillness (the gliding court walk), fan handling (props honesty: paired pleated fans — practice fans or any folding fans work; feathered mulberry buchae when you're ready), and single-fan phrases. Gutgeori jangdan, the lilting 12/8 that carries it, is in the Rhythm Trainer.

seasons.finale: Film yourself breathing and swaying with the gutgeori jangdan — the 12/8 lilt carried in the knees.
Film fan handling both hands — open, close, flutter, the wrist rolls — crisp openings, soft carriage.
Film the curved arm lines and the gliding walk — moving like water, fans breathing with you.
Film a single-fan solo phrase — walk, turn, bloom, settle — unhurried and curved throughout.
See buchaechum whole: a live performance or full recording of the ensemble flowers — then find a Korean dance class if the road allows.

attributes.name: Fan-wrist control L1
attributes.test: 20 clean fan openings and closings each hand (any folding fan) — crisp snap open, silent close, forearm quiet

attributes.name: Court carriage L1
attributes.test: 60s of the gliding walk — tall, serene, steps invisible under a long skirt (real or imagined)

attributes.name: Jangdan ear L1
attributes.test: sway and breathe with gutgeori through one full track, knees carrying the lilt, never squaring it

nodes.name: Gutgeori jangdan — the lilting 12/8
checkpoints: Korean traditional music moves in jangdan — rhythmic cycles kept by the janggu drum; gutgeori is the graceful, lilting 12/8 that carries buchaechum, and it's in this app's Rhythm Trainer
the pulse is breathed, not counted: the body rises and settles with it — knees soft, chest buoyant
listen for the janggu's low kung and high deok trading — the cycle's shape lives between them

nodes.name: Heung and the vertical breath
checkpoints: Korean dance rides a vertical breath — a gentle rise (inhale) and settle (exhale) that never stops, the engine under every movement
'heung' — often glossed as the lift of shared joy — is the feeling the breath carries; described here with humility, learned truly from Korean teachers and audiences
practice: one minute of nothing but breathing with the jangdan; that IS the technique

nodes.name: Kim Baek-bong — the woman who made it
checkpoints: buchaechum was created in 1954 by KIM BAEK-BONG — a named choreographer who drew on shamanic ritual aesthetics and court dance to build a new work that became a Korean national icon
her academy and designated lineage carry the dance today; performances that credit her honor the norm this whole app enforces
a living counter-example to 'folk dances have no author' — some do, and she is one, and she is a woman whose name deserves saying

nodes.name: The ensemble art — flowers, waves, butterflies
checkpoints: buchaechum's iconic images — the blooming flower, the rolling wave, the butterfly — are built from many dancers' fans moving as one
the full dance is ensemble art learned with teams and teachers: Korean cultural centers and dance academies teach it worldwide
this pack is the honest doorway: breath, line, fans and solo phrases here; the flower blooms in a room of dancers

nodes.name: Fan handling
nodes.anchor: the fans are the voice — learn to let them speak
checkpoints: open with a crisp snap, close in silence — both hands, until either hand can do either job mid-phrase
the flutter: small fast wrist tremors that make the fan shimmer like wings
props honesty: paired pleated fans — practice fans or any folding fans to learn; feathered mulberry-paper buchae when the hands are ready
carry the fans as extensions of the arm's curve, never gripped like tools
mistakes: openings that wilt instead of snap
white-knuckle grip (the fan should look weightless)

nodes.name: The curved line & the gliding walk
checkpoints: every arm path curves — no corners anywhere; the fan draws arcs the eye can rest on
the gliding walk: small hidden steps under a serene carriage, moving like water finding level
rise-and-settle breath under everything; the walk breathes even when the fans are still
the persian pack's arm framing and the flamenco braceo are distant cousins — the curve discipline transfers
mistakes: bouncing the walk (the glide is the whole illusion)
straight-armed fan carries (the curve is the aesthetic)

nodes.name: Eokkaechum — the shoulder's lilt
checkpoints: Korean dance carries a signature shoulder impulse — eokkaechum, the 'shoulder dance' — a gentle rise-and-release riding the jangdan, joy expressed from the shoulders
it comes from the breath, never from a shrug: the inhale lifts the shoulders a whisper, the exhale melts them
layer it under the fans and the glide; it's the difference between carrying the dance and wearing it
mistakes: mechanical shoulder pops (this is a lilt, not an isolation drill — the popping pack lives elsewhere)

nodes.name: Single-fan solo phrases
checkpoints: compose short phrases: glide in, a turn with the fan sweeping a full arc, a flutter bloom, a settled close
phrase with the gutgeori cycle — begin and resolve on the jangdan's breath
solo phrases are real buchaechum vocabulary; the ensemble magnifies them, it doesn't replace them

nodes.name: The ensemble forms (with a team)
checkpoints: the flower, the wave, the butterfly — learned with a team and a teacher, where spacing and breath synchronize many dancers into one image
Korean cultural centers, university teams and academies teach ensemble buchaechum worldwide
arrive with your breath, your fans and Kim Baek-bong's name — the three things every teacher hopes for

nodes.name: The solo phrase — filmed
checkpoints: one gutgeori track: gliding entrance, two composed phrases, a flutter bloom, a settled ending — single fan, all curves
watch it back at half speed: any corners? any bounce? the water test
credit the creator on camera — 'buchaechum, created by Kim Baek-bong, 1954' — practicing the norm

nodes.name: See the flower bloom
checkpoints: watch a full ensemble buchaechum — live if a Korean cultural festival is near, complete recording otherwise; watch the BREATHING synchronize, not just the fans
if the road allows, take a Korean dance class — the jangdan feels different when a janggu is in the room
the flower you watched is dozens of solo phrases breathing together; you now hold one of them
